signals.text: Our curriculum is the progression model, which well-sequenced and incremental, setting out an increasingly technical, constructive and expressive knowledge of music..
These will be embedded and further developed in Upper KS2, alongside Reading and Writing, gradually progressing onto more complex language concepts and greater learner autonomy.
At Laleham, our ambitious, inclusive and bespoke music curriculum is delivered by a music specialist and meets all components of the Model Music Curriculum (2021).

signals.text: Wellbeing At Laleham C of E primary School, our vision is to develop a school community where children can enjoy a welcoming, secure, happy and healthy environment, where everyone can develop self-confidence, self-esteem, self-motivation, independence, compassion, tolerance and understanding of others.

Morning Activity Breakfast Club and After School Club Sportive Kids - Breakfast Club Sportive Kids offer a morning wraparound service from Reception to Y6 at Laleham Primary School, providing a safe, welcoming and enjoyable environment for children before the school day.

We are pleased to be able to offer a morning wraparound service from Reception to Y6 at Laleham Primary School, providing a safe, welcoming and enjoyable environment for children before the school day.

Clubs
At Laleham, we strive to offer as many extra-curricular and enrichment opportunities for the children. We aspire to cultivate their personal talents and interests and so they can access a culturally rich and rounded learning experience. To achieve this, we enter a range of intra-school and inter-school sporting competitions. We believe that competitive activity is vital; we attend competitions such as Mixed Hockey, Tag Rugby, Mixed indoor athletics, Netball, and Football.
To promote sports further, we provide and promote a variety of early morning and after-school clubs. We have worked hard to expand our extra-curricular sporting provision and offer a wide range of opportunities for the children to participate in. We offer choir, cricket, football, netball and cheerleading clubs.
Club Allocation Approach for School Organised Sports Clubs
Following the registration of interest, we shall allocate clubs taking several factors into consideration, including (but not limited to, or in order of preference): number of places, gender, pupil premium, activity level, previous commitment, social needs. We shall continue to operate waiting lists. The decision of the school will be final; the nature of the factors that we will be considering mean that we are unable to share our reasoning in individual cases. Please trust that we know and value the children and are doing our absolute best to ensure they all get the opportunities that they need.
Every year, our clubs are oversubscribed; we see this as a fantastic reflection of the quality that we offer and the supportiveness of our parents and carers in encouraging participation. We recognise that some children will be disappointed and we ask for parent/carer support in helping children to be accepting. There are a finite number of places and that means not everyone is able to be included. We recognise that this may be quite a new experience for many of the children as during curriculum time everyone is always catered for. Please use this as an opportunity to support your child to develop acceptance and resilience as these are important life skills that are going to stand them in good stead moving forwards. We will continue to operate waiting lists for children who miss out or apply late; this has proved successful in previous years.

pageCache.pageTitle: Laleham CofE Primary School - Careers Fair
pageCache.text:
Careers Fair
Following the successful launch of the Laleham Careers Fair in 2023, we held a Careers Day on Friday 28th February 2025.
For more information on the careers day we held in February 2025 please click here
Why do a careers fair? We want our children to:
What will it look like?
On Friday 28th February, we are inviting all children to dress up in costume wearing the clothes typically related to their dream job when they grow up. Throughout the day, the children will take part in various activities in class which will inspire and open up their minds to the many possibilities they have in life.
Children in Years 2-6 will also take part in the careers fair. The hall will be transformed with different stands from the world of work; they will get the opportunity to talk to adults from the various business and organisations on show. Some stands will have practical demonstrations, and even freebies!
Would your business or organisation be able to run a stall on the careers fair? Perhaps you work for a large company, run a business, work in the public sector, or are retired from a profession? We will supply a table and chairs, and electric points can be made available for a laptop or equipment. You could bring along vertical banners, hands-on activities, leaflets and freebies, and can have one or more adults to help run the stall. We’ll even provide refreshments.
Remember, the purpose is to inspire pupils and engage with them in thinking about their aspirations.
Do you have more information if I am interested in helping?
If you have any questions or need to find out more, please email info@laleham.surrey.sch.uk
The date is Friday 28th February 2025

Modern Foreign Languages
At Laleham C of E Primary School, we provide children with the opportunity to develop a foreign language. We want to deliver a curriculum which is accessible to all and that will maximise the outcomes for every child so that they not only know more but remember more and understand more. We believe that children need to enjoy lessons, be engaged and challenged in order for them to understand, retain knowledge and progress. Our aim is that all children in KS2 will assess quality teaching of French and leave Laleham confident and motivated to continue to further develop their skills into the next stage of their education and beyond.

Music
At Laleham C of E Primary School we aim to encourage and foster in all children a lifelong love of and connection with music, through active involvement and engagement at all levels. Singing is the foundation of all our musical learning and through this our children discover how to listen and respond to different styles of music. The children’s creative responses become more formalised in KS2 when they begin to experiment with form, structure, texture and the interrelated dimensions of music. Alongside this we aim to also teach children that music reflects our culture and society which enables children to better understand the world we live in.
All children have the opportunity to further develop their musicianship skills in weekly singing sessions where pupils listen, learn and perform a wide variety of assembly and worship songs. During these sessions, children develop their vocal skills, are challenged to sing in two-parts and our young instrumentalists also have the opportunity to perform to others.
Laleham has always been a musical school and has a long-established and thriving choir which is open to children from years 2 to 6. In previous years the choir has participated in the annual Surrey Border Schools concerts in Princes Hall, Aldershot, and in March last year they were due to sing in Dorking Halls as part of the North Surrey Primary Music Festival. Even during this challenging year of Covid restrictions, we have continued to run weekly choir rehearsals with smaller groups of children. We also welcome Surrey Arts into our school who offer a range of instrumental lessons to children.
We strongly believe that every child is musical, and a musical school is a happy school. Music has the power to inspire us, bring us together and make us smile.

Wellbeing
At Laleham C of E primary School, our vision is to develop a school community where children can enjoy a welcoming, secure, happy and healthy environment, where everyone can develop self-confidence, self-esteem, self-motivation, independence, compassion, tolerance and understanding of others.
At Laleham, we support the emotional health and wellbeing of our pupils.
At our school we know that everyone experiences life challenges that can make us vulnerable and at times, anyone may need additional emotional support. We take the view that positive mental health is everybody’s business and that we all have a role to play.
We promote a mentally healthy environment through:-
